content:
Hi, I have recently installed Lean 4 and it takes a long time whenever a project needs to import Mathlib.
I have tried running lake exe cache get but it seems that the cache is already there:
"Current branch: HEAD
Using cache (Azure) from origin: (some leanprover-community/mathlib4)
No files to download
Already decompressed 8477 file(s)"
Still even after lake exe cache get, the files need 10 minutes or more to import Mathlib every time.
Is there any way to solve this problem?

What is it you are doing that leads you to this step ? If I just clone Mathlib and build it once even without cache get, why is it building again for you?

FYI If you are editing files that are imported a lot, after your edit you will have to rebuild every file you’ve impacted. Depending on the file this could take ten minutes , or it can even take an hour.

I started a new project and try to import Mathlib, the file has no dependencies apart from Mathlib itself, but it is loadly very slowly (Like the Lean Infoview keeps loading for ten minutes).
I searched on the web and it say maybe its a cache problem so I tried that command.

The other thing is, if I start another file also just with import Mathlib (and no other files), it also loads for a long time even when the first file (which is unrelated) already loads Mathlib successfully.
What are your computer hardware specifications?

It's a desktop with intel i5 CPU and 16 GB RAM.
I also tried with a laptop with similar spec and it encounters similar problems.

Tom Leung said:

intel i5 CPU

Which generation?

desktop is i5-7400
laptop is i5-1035G1
That means the desktop is 9 years old, aka older than Mathlib itself

actually what is the recommended spec for running lean 4 with mathlib?
I used the same laptop for Lean 3 a few years before and don't have the same problem.
So Lean 4 way more demanding in terms of spec?
Mathlib is a growing project so comparing between years doesn't say much, but AFAIK Lean 4 should be more performant than Lean 3
See e.g. this graph of growth of Mathlib over time (number of files & lines of code), and this graph for how the performance of Mathlib4 changed in recent years
I think you shouldn't be surprised that running modern software on a 9-year-old PC takes a while.
For best-effort, have you tried using the module system? If your file starts with the line module you save around 50% of the RAM needed to import mathlib
Is your project in a Google drive / dropbox / ... folder?
it's local files
I am not familar with the module system. So you just add module at the start?
Yes, and also public before every import

I use an M1 MacBook Air with 16GB of memory and never had any problem. I just tried public import Mathlib and it took no more than half a minute. M1 MBA is faster than Intel i5, but I seriously doubt that the difference can be 10x.

Ching-Tsun Chou said:

M1 MBA is faster than Intel i5, but I seriously doubt that the difference can be 10x.

Considering the difference in time , it may genuinely be close to 10x. Maybe not in isolation , that is if you somehow get an i5 in there with all same HW . But if the desktop is old overall , the amount of RAM isn't a good indicator anymore. Either way using process management with whatever OS you should be able to figure out if its something thats not HW capacity related.

Tom Leung said:

I used the same laptop for Lean 3 a few years before and don't have the same problem.

Issue is with Mathlib rather than Lean really since thats the premise, so Mathlib3 vs Mathlib4 which has grown dramatically since then.

Amount of files has grown by a factor, check out the graph at https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib_stats.html

Eric Wieser said:

Is your project in a Google drive / dropbox / ... folder?

For what it's worth, the following is one metric to detect such problematic file systems

$ lake env time lean Mathlib.lean --stats | grep modules
number of imported modules:            37310
number of memory-mapped modules:       37307
1.45user 0.80system 0:02.35elapsed 95%CPU

Those two numbers should be identical or (now that Mathlib has further grown, as mentioned) at least very close together
Oh, I'd assumed the issue was just that these filesystems were slow, not that they didn't support mmapping

Tom Leung said:

It's a desktop with intel i5 CPU and 16 GB RAM.
I also tried with a laptop with similar spec and it encounters similar problems.

What's your operating system? Windows is known to be slow due to antivirus, etc.

Eric Wieser said:

Oh, I'd assumed the issue was just that these filesystems were slow, not that they didn't support mmapping

Both, either? Who knows
Yes the next question in the standard checklist for this issue is "do you have an antivirus running eg Microsoft Defender? Try switching it off".

Jz Pan said:

Tom Leung said:

It's a desktop with intel i5 CPU and 16 GB RAM.
I also tried with a laptop with similar spec and it encounters similar problems.

What's your operating system? Windows is known to be slow due to antivirus, etc.

Yes it is running on Windows, but I am not sure what antivirus it is running since the computers are provided by the school, and those I cannot turn off. I am now trying to see if I can install Lean with Mathlib on my private computer.

How long does it take to decompress all files in lake exe cache get? For example, on my own Windows computer with 8GB ram, it will take 600 seconds due to antivirus and inefficiency of Windows. But on another Linux computer it only takes 4 seconds.

Maybe you can try install Lean4 on WSL2 then asks your VSCode on Windows to connect to it. Unfortunately it is an advanced topic, but you can ask Google and it will provide a step-by-step walkthrough (at least last time I use this to install it on another Windows PC).

Tom Leung said:

Yes it is running on Windows, but I am not sure what antivirus it is running since the computers are provided by the school, and those I cannot turn off.

I was in exactly this situation but I could still tell Windows Defender to stop scanning the relevant directories, which solved the problem for me.
